entries.originalText: For no worldly good whatsoever, and for the love of no man, must anything be done which is evil, but for the help of the suffering a good work must sometimes be postponed, or be changed for a better; for herein a good work is not destroyed, but improved.
entries.modernizedText: For no worldly good whatsoever and for the love of no person must anything evil be done, but to help someone who suffers, a good work must sometimes be postponed or changed for a better one; for in this a good work is not destroyed, but improved.

entries.originalText: Without charity no work profiteth, but whatsoever is done in charity, however small and of no reputation it be, bringeth forth good fruit; for God verily considereth what a man is able to do, more than the greatness of what he doth.
entries.modernizedText: Without charity no work profits, but whatever is done in charity, however small and without reputation it may be, brings forth good fruit; for God truly considers what a person is able to do more than the greatness of what he does.

entries.originalText: He doth much who loveth much.
entries.modernizedText: The person who loves much does much.

entries.originalText: He doth much who doth well.
entries.modernizedText: The person who does well does much.

entries.originalText: He doth well who ministereth to the public good rather than to his own.
entries.modernizedText: The person who serves the public good rather than his own does well.

entries.originalText: Oftentimes that seemeth to be charity which is rather carnality, because it springeth from natural inclination, self-will, hope of repayment, desire of gain.
entries.modernizedText: What seems to be charity is often instead carnality, because it springs from natural inclination, self-will, hope of repayment, or desire for gain.

entries.originalText: He who hath true and perfect charity, in no wise seeketh his own good, but desireth that God alone be altogether glorified.
entries.modernizedText: The person who has true and perfect charity in no way seeks his own good, but desires that God alone be altogether glorified.

entries.originalText: He envieth none, because he longeth for no selfish joy; nor doth he desire to rejoice in himself, but longeth to be blessed in God as the highest good.
entries.modernizedText: He envies no one, because he longs for no selfish joy; nor does he desire to rejoice in himself, but longs to be blessed in God as the highest good.

entries.originalText: He ascribeth good to none save to God only, the Fountain whence all good proceedeth, and the End, the Peace, the joy of all Saints.
entries.modernizedText: He ascribes good to no one except God alone, the Fountain from which all good proceeds, and the End, the Peace, the joy of all Saints.

entries.originalText: Oh, he who hath but a spark of true charity, hath verily learned that all worldly things are full of vanity.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, the person who has even a spark of true charity has truly learned that all worldly things are full of vanity.
